bit_string_types.name: opcode
bit_string_types.description: RRQ and WRQ packets (opcodes 1 and 2 respectively) have the format shown in Figure 5-1.

bit_string_types.name: filename
bit_string_types.description: The file name is a sequence of bytes in netascii terminated by a zero byte.

bit_string_types.name: mode
bit_string_types.description: The mode field contains the string "netascii", "octet", or "mail" (or any combination of upper and lower case, such as "NETASCII", NetAscii", etc.) in netascii indicating the three modes defined in the protocol.

bit_string_types.name: opcode
bit_string_types.description: DATA packets (opcode = 3) have a block number and data field.

bit_string_types.name: block_number
bit_string_types.description: The block numbers on data packets begin with one and increase by one for each new block of data.

bit_string_types.name: data
bit_string_types.description: The data field is from zero to 512 bytes long. If it is 512 bytes long, the block is not the last block of data; if it is from zero to 511 bytes long, it signals the end of the transfer.

bit_string_types.name: opcode
bit_string_types.description: Figure 5-3 depicts an ACK packet; the opcode is 4.

bit_string_types.name: block_number
bit_string_types.description: The block number in an ACK echoes the block number of the DATA packet being acknowledged. A WRQ is acknowledged with an ACK packet having a block number of zero.

bit_string_types.name: opcode
bit_string_types.description: An ERROR packet (opcode 5) takes the form depicted in Figure 5-4.

bit_string_types.name: error_code
bit_string_types.description: The error code is an integer indicating the nature of the error. A table of values and meanings is given in the appendix.

bit_string_types.name: err_msg
bit_string_types.description: The error message is intended for human consumption, and should be in netascii. Like all other strings, it is terminated with a zero byte.
